answer_1.quote: We also evaluate BART+KILM on QA tasks and is less prone to hallucination on tasks such as knowledge‑grounded response generation. ... We also test on summarization datasets (CNN/DailyMail, XSUM) and on appositive generation.
answer_1.outputs: Generated summaries, knowledge‑grounded responses, appositive phrases, answer spans

answer_2.quote: The generated responses are evaluated with PPL, ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2 metrics. ... We also use unigram F1 and METEOR for appositive generation and report EM/F1 for entity description probing.

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation is done among a group of experts fluent in English... Pairwise A/B testing is utilized to compare the performances of BART before and after KILM. For ApposCorpus we evaluate Is Appositive (Ap.), Preference (Pref.) and Not Hallucinated (NH.). For WoW we evaluate Fluency (Flu.), Informativeness (Info.) and Not Hallucinated (NH.).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were shown the same context and two generated options, then asked to choose generation A, B, both, or neither based on the specified criteria (e.g., appositive presence, preference, hallucination for appositives; fluency, informativeness, hallucination for dialogue).
